title: Height-one principal criterion for unique factorization
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] integral domain. The following are equivalent: (i) $R$ is a unique factorization domain: every nonzero element of $R$ is a unit times a finite product of prime elements, uniquely up to order and association; (ii) every height-one prime ideal of $R$ is principal, where a prime $\mathfrak p$ has height one if $\mathfrak p\ne0$ and no prime ideal lies strictly between $0$ and $\mathfrak p$.

mathlib_match.how: exact: lines 87–89 under CommRing R and IsDomain R (line 26) and IsNoetherianRing R (line 67); tagged stacks 0AFT at line 86. UniqueFactorizationMonoid R is the usual unique factorization property (UniqueFactorizationDomain/Defs.lean:121–143). For a prime ideal, height is the supremum of lengths of strict prime chains below it (Ideal/Height.lean:29–44); in a domain the zero prime is the least prime, so height = 1 means precisely nonzero with no prime strictly between zero and it. Submodule.IsPrincipal is precisely generated by one element. No additional hypothesis or comparison of different algebraic notions is required.
